newsitem.title: KENYA: African ministers in dark about Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: African ministers in dark about Zaire talks.

text.p: African ministers returning from a peace mission to Kinshasa on Thursday appeared in the dark about talks in Cape Town to bring together warring parties in Zaire.

The foreign ministers of South Africa, Kenya, Tanzania and Zimbabwe said at Nairobi airport they expected to receive some details of the talks announced by President Nelson Mandela when they returned home.
"Now we are returning we will get the details," South African Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo told a news conference following talks in Kinshasa on Wednesday with Zairean ministers.

Asked if they saw any evidence the Zairean government was speaking with more than one voice because officials in Kinshasa appeared to know nothing the preparations for the Cape Town talks, the ministers said those they had met appeared united.
"They all seemed to be speaking on the same frequency. So we didn't see any evidence of divided opinion or divided positions," said Tanzanian Foreign Minister Jakaya Mrisho Kikwete.
The delegation met Zaire's prime minister, deputy prime minister and ministers of foreign affairs, defence and interior.

The ministers said Zaire's government seemed to have no major problems with a five point peace plan the U.N. Security Council adopted on Tuesday although Kinshasa said it was too timid for not condemning what it holds are the foreign aggressors.

But they said Zaire demanded a total withdrawal of foreign forces from eastern Zaire before it would attend a suggested enlarged summit in Nairobi on the conflict. Zaire boycotted two earlier summits.

"They don't want to come to Nairobi to discuss a mechanism (for a withdrawal of forces). Before they come to Nairobi they want to be sure that there has been a total withdrawal of foreign forces," said Kenyan Foreign Minister Kalonzo Musyoka.
He added the Zaireans were "going out of their way" to press for a mechanism to monitor such a pullout before any new summit.

He said Kinshasa wanted African leaders to concentrate on the question of securing a withdrawal of foreign forces and said that then the Zaireans would settle their own problems through elections, even in the east which is currently held by rebels.
"Our (diplomatic) effort is not aimed at removing President Mobutu from power. That must be every clear...It is the Zaireans who will decide that issue," said Nzo of South Africa.
Musyoka said the African foreign ministers had stressed in Kinshasa the commitment of African leaders to preserve the territorial integrity of Zaire, the third largest country in the continent.
